from: We started testing the new CRM in March, and we are still testing it.
frame: We ___ the new CRM since March.

ok.de: Richtig: „since March“ und die Arbeit läuft noch → have been testing.
ok.en: Right: “since March” + still going → have been testing.

wrong.de: Das Schlüsselwort been muss unverändert in der Lücke stehen.
wrong.en: The key word been must stay unchanged in the gap.

wrong.de: Present Continuous passt nicht zu since: Es fehlt have been.
wrong.en: Present Continuous does not go with since: have been is missing.

wrong.de: Mit been und -ing: have been testing. Hier ist das Schlüsselwort Pflicht.
wrong.en: With been and -ing: have been testing. The key word is required here.

from: I started waiting for the invoice on Monday, and I am still waiting.

ok.de: Richtig: Start am Montag und noch im Gange → have been waiting since Monday.
ok.en: Right: started Monday, still going → have been waiting since Monday.

wrong.de: Das Schlüsselwort since muss unverändert in der Lücke stehen.
wrong.en: The key word since must stay unchanged in the gap.

wrong.de: Nach since steht kein Present Continuous, sondern have been waiting.
wrong.en: After since use have been waiting, not the Present Continuous.

wrong.de: Ohne been fehlt die Form: have been waiting since Monday.
wrong.en: been is missing: have been waiting since Monday.

wrong.de: Past Simple passt nicht zu since: have waited oder have been waiting.
wrong.en: Past Simple does not go with since: have waited or have been waiting.

prompt: We are working on the integration since last October.
fixed: We have been working on the integration since last October.

ok.de: Der Fehler: „are working“ passt nicht zu since. Richtig: have been working.
ok.en: The error: “are working” does not go with since. Correct: have been working.

wrong.de: Doch, hier steckt ein Fehler: since verlangt den Blick zurück.
wrong.en: There is an error: since needs the look back.

wrong.de: Der Fehler liegt bei „are working“: So klingt das deutsche Präsens, English braucht have been.
wrong.en: The error is “are working”: that is the German present, English needs have been.

prompt: She is the account manager for this client since 2020.
fixed: She has been the account manager for this client since 2020.

ok.de: Der Fehler: „is“ passt nicht zu since 2020. Richtig: has been.
ok.en: The error: “is” does not go with since 2020. Correct: has been.

wrong.de: Doch, hier ist ein Fehler: since 2020 verlangt Present Perfect.
wrong.en: There is an error: since 2020 needs the Present Perfect.

wrong.de: Der Fehler liegt bei „is“: Für „seit 2020“ braucht Englisch has been.
wrong.en: The error is “is”: for “seit 2020” English needs has been.

prompt: Our engineers have been fixing the login bug since early this morning.

ok.de: Stimmt: „since early this morning“ + have been fixing, die Arbeit läuft noch.
ok.en: Correct: “since early this morning” + have been fixing, the work is ongoing.

wrong.de: Hier ist alles richtig: since verlangt have been fixing, und das steht da.
wrong.en: This is correct: since needs have been fixing, and that is what we have.

a: We have been working on the proposal since Monday.
b: We worked on the proposal on Monday.

q.en: Which sentence says the work on the proposal is still going on?

ok.de: Richtig: Satz a. have been working since Monday reicht bis jetzt.
ok.en: Right: sentence a. have been working since Monday reaches up to now.

wrong.de: In b steht Past Simple mit „on Monday“: Das ist vorbei.
wrong.en: Sentence b uses the Past Simple with “on Monday”: that is over.

wrong.de: Nicht gleich: a läuft noch, b ist abgeschlossen.
wrong.en: Not the same: a is ongoing, b is finished.

from: We started negotiating two weeks ago, and we are still negotiating.

ok.en: Right: two weeks is a length of time → have been negotiating for.

wrong.en: The key word for must stay unchanged in the gap.

wrong.de: since braucht einen Zeitpunkt; two weeks ist eine Zeitspanne, also for.
wrong.en: since needs a point in time; two weeks is a length of time, so for.

wrong.de: Ohne been fehlt die Form: have been negotiating for.
wrong.en: been is missing: have been negotiating for.

from: He started working remotely in September and still works remotely.

wrong.de: Ohne been fehlt die Form: has been working remotely since.
wrong.en: been is missing: has been working remotely since.

prompt: We have been waiting on the approval since three days.

wrong.en: There is an error: since does not go with a length of time.

wrong.de: Der Fehler liegt bei „since three“: Deutsch „seit drei Tagen“ braucht hier for.

a: I have lived in Munich for two years.

wrong.en: In a the activity is in focus; whether it is finished stays open.

wrong.de: Nicht gleich: a lässt offen, ob fertig, b sagt es klar.
